source: APPP / MAFF-JICA — Rice Seed Production Manual (សៀវភៅមគ្គទេសក៍ផលិតកម្មពូជស្រូវ), 2014, Agricultural Productivity Promotion Project in West Tonle Sap, p.18
text: A small pest (roughly 1 mm, described in the manual similarly to a mite/thrips) can damage rice seedlings at the nursery stage, causing seedlings to become stunted and curled/twisted. Signs of thrips damage in the nursery show as patches of stunted, twisted seedlings. Recommended prevention: cover the nursery bed with fine mesh netting to physically exclude the pest from reaching the seedlings; the manual also notes planting marigold-type flowers (ផ្កា) near/around the nursery as an additional control measure. The APPP project treats this pest as an important, nationally-recognized nursery pest and recommends netting as the primary control method.
